trust_decision.summary: HTML returned by an external oEmbed provider that is emitted as a non-sandboxed <iframe> into the host document must carry only allowlisted attributes (no on*, no srcdoc, no style/class/id) and must not have a javascript:/data:/vbscript:/file: src; the decision is made in EmbedShortcodeProvider::sandboxHtml's already-an-iframe branch.

landing_point.why: It is the single line where provider-supplied iframe HTML is returned into the template unmodified (the '<= 2 HTML tags' fast path), and it is the only source line the published diff changes.

fix_sites.entry_point: ShortcodeParser '[embed]' tag -> EmbedShortcodeProvider::handle_shortcode() (registered in _config.php:15), via embeddableToHtml() -> videoEmbed() -> sandboxHtml()

EmbedShortcodeProvider::embeddableToHtml() public static API (called directly by the project's own test at tests/php/View/Shortcodes/EmbedShortcodeProviderTest.php:383) -> videoEmbed() -> sandboxHtml()
fix_sites.module_kind: new private helper on the same View-layer shortcode provider

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The sandboxing that gates the whole attribute filter has a documented opt-out (private static $domains_excluded_from_sandboxing, src/View/Shortcodes/EmbedShortcodeProvider.php:33-38 and the early return at :382-384), so a solver can argue that an excluded domain, or a URL that merely ends with an excluded domain, was deliberately never covered by the advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Mainstream provider embeds must keep allow / allowfullscreen / webkitallowfullscreen / mozallowfullscreen / referrerpolicy / title / frameborder / scrolling and a schemeless or protocol-relative src; an over-broad fix (strip everything but src/width/height, or a DOM rewrite that drops valueless attributes) breaks the existing YouTube, Vimeo and SoundCloud expectations at the pinned commit. A second, finer trap: an attribute prefixed with U+00A0 is inert to browsers and must be left untouched, so a filter that treats \s with the /u modifier as a separator changes output it should not.

O6_input_shapes: double-quoted, single-quoted and unquoted (bare) attribute values
whitespace separators, tab separators, whitespace around '=', and '/' as an attribute separator (<iframe/onload=...>)
a '>' inside a quoted attribute value, both in a kept and in a stripped attribute
multiple event-handler attributes on the same tag
attributes that are not event handlers at all: srcdoc, style, class, id, data-* , name, csp
src scheme variants: javascript:, data:text/html, vbscript:, entity/control-char obfuscated (java	script:), protocol-relative (//host), and normal https

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Cache hit: handle_shortcode returns the stored embed HTML verbatim from the PSR-16 cache before embeddableToHtml()/sandboxHtml() ever runs, so the new attribute filter is never applied to a cached value.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Cached HTML is pre-existing stored data, not something this request built; a separate cache-invalidation API exists (flushCachedShortcodes, :315-340) and a solver can say invalidating or re-filtering the cache is the site developer's job after an upgrade.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~290 lines above the landing point, different lifecycle stage (read path vs build path)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Domain exclusion matches on a bare suffix: str_ends_with($domain, $excludedDomain) with no '.' boundary, so a host that merely ends with an excluded domain (notexample.com against excluded example.com) takes the early return at :382-384 and its provider-supplied iframe is emitted with on*/srcdoc/style intact, bypassing the new filter entirely.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Subdomain matching is deliberate and documented ('This will also exclude any subdomains', :33-38); the advisory is about iframe attributes, not about how the exclusion list is matched, and any host in that list is an administrator's trust decision.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~44 lines below the landing point, different concern (config domain matching rather than HTML filtering)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A photo provider path that renders provider-supplied HTML (not just the page URL) into the main document, sharing the same attribute filter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: photoEmbed() already receives provider-derived values and renders a tag straight into the document from a .ss template; a maintainer adding oEmbed photo markup passthrough would need exactly the same allowlist, and the copy would look like the natural next provider type.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An 'audio' branch that is classified by getType() but never rendered, becoming a new route into videoEmbed()/sandboxHtml().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getType() already returns 'audio' explicitly (:95-97) yet embeddableToHtml() has no branch for it and silently falls back to linkEmbed(); completing that branch is the obvious follow-up work and invites the same sanitisation question.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second, Core-level attribute blocklist doing the same job, extended with the iframe-specific names the embed filter strips (srcdoc, style) and the src-scheme check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: XssSanitiser is the framework's documented HTML-fragment sanitiser (sanitiseString(), :45-50) and already owns an on* blocklist and a src-scheme check (:186-206); a maintainer cleaning up 'the XSS sanitiser' could plausibly extend it there instead of hand-rolling a regex in the shortcode provider.

O9_family: CWE-79 cross-site scripting (HTML attribute injection into a non-sandboxed iframe)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip only on* attributes from the raw iframe with a small regex (or reuse the existing XssSanitiser::sanitiseString()), leaving srcdoc, style/class/id, and javascript:/data: src values in place.
